back_translation: The burden-oracle concerning Egypt: Behold, the LORD is mounted on a swift cloud and is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt quake before His face, and the heart of the Egyptians melts within them.
"I will incite Egypt against Egypt: brother will fight against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will be poured out empty from within them, and I will swallow up their plans. They will go consult the idols and the spirits of the dead, the mediums and the spiritists.
And I will hand Egypt over into the hand of a harsh master, and a fierce king will rule over them," — thus the Sovereign Master, the LORD of Hosts, has declared.
The waters of the sea will be drained away, and the River will be parched dry and scorched.
The canals will stink with rot; the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up; the reeds and rushes will rot away.
The bare rushes along the Nile, at the mouth of the river, and all the sown fields beside the Nile will wither, blow away, and be no more.
The fishermen will lament and mourn — all who cast a hook into the Nile; and those who spread nets on the water's surface will languish.
The workers in combed flax will be ashamed, and the weavers of fine white cloth will turn pale.
The pillars of the land will be crushed, and all the wage-workers will be grieved at heart.
The princes of Zoan are utter fools; the wisest counselors of Pharaoh give worthless counsel. How dare you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of sages, a son of ancient kings"?
Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you and reveal what the LORD of Hosts has purposed against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools; the princes of Noph are deceived; the cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has poured into her a spirit of dizziness, and they have made Egypt stagger in everything she does, like a drunkard staggering in his own vomit.
And there will be no work that Egypt can accomplish — whether by head or tail, palm frond or reed.
In that day the Egyptians will be like women: they will tremble with fear before the hand of the LORD of Hosts raised over them.
And the land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone who hears its name mentioned will dread it, because of the plan that the LORD of Hosts has purposed against Egypt.
In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of Hosts. One city will be called the City of the Sun.
In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a sacred pillar to the LORD at its border.
It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of Hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of oppressors, He will send them a Savior and a Defender, and He will rescue them.
The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and in that day Egypt will know the LORD. They will worship with sacrifice and grain offering; they will make vows to the LORD and fulfill them.
The LORD will strike Egypt — striking and then healing — and they will turn back to the LORD; He will listen to their pleas and heal them.
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will come to Egypt and the Egyptians to Assyria, and the Egyptians will worship together with the Assyrians.
In that day Israel will be a third alongside Egypt and Assyria — a blessing in the midst of the earth.
The LORD of Hosts has blessed them, saying: "Blessed be Egypt My people, Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance."
